pipeline.title: Prepare a repeatable state
pipeline.meaning: A recorded procedure sets the state used to predict the next detector records. Here it prepares equal, same-phase amplitudes in two bins.
pipeline.graphic: Two neighbouring bins glow; their phase arrows point together. A preparation record labels this setting.

pipeline.title: Choose which question the apparatus asks
pipeline.meaning: The apparatus couples an observable to output ports. Direct routing reads spatial bins; a Fourier analyser combines phases to read momentum bins.
pipeline.graphic: One packet splits into two alternative apparatus drawings, a direct channel and a four-path phase analyser. These are alternative experiments.

pipeline.title: A detector leaves a record
pipeline.meaning: Each port has a Born weight. One retained outcome conditions subsequent predictions. Show all ports, including the zero-weight port; show no-click or failure outcomes when the physical instrument has them.
pipeline.graphic: Four detector cells, a highlighted example click and a histogram of the complete outcome weights.

pipeline.title: Compare and share the record
pipeline.meaning: Observers verify and copy a distinguishable record label. Agreement keeps its probability law; it does not vote an outcome into existence or create the mass.
pipeline.graphic: Two ledgers carry the same verified label, joined by a compare/check line; the unselected branches remain in the complete probability diagram.

captions.wave: Amplitudes spread and acquire relative phase. At an output they add before their squared magnitude becomes a probability. A missing count can be destructive interference.
captions.uncertainty: A sharp position record gives this state a broad momentum distribution. Momentum has a probability law, not a single sharp value. A sharp momentum mode spreads position.
captions.Born: For a complete instrument, p(r)=Tr(rho K_r†K_r). The chosen state and instrument determine the weights; keeping every outcome makes them sum to one.
captions.conditioning: After a positive-weight record r, predictions use K_r rho K_r†/p(r). In this projective example that is the Lüders update; Born weights alone do not select the update.
captions.consensus: A record fixes the shared outcome of this experiment. It does not assign sharp values to every incompatible observable.
captions.source_scope: Native closed histories derive a positive Born-form functional. Implementing arbitrary complex effects as native detector events requires an additional operational bridge.
captions.continuum_scope: A specified ordered-spin field constructs position and its own translation momentum with Delta X Delta P >= hbar/2 on the stated domain. The particle, source clock and laboratory-unit identifications are separate.

proof_links.label: Particle paper section 5.19, position and probe uncertainty

illustration_scope: Four-bin supplied state and Fourier projective instruments. No universal position PVM for all species, physical momentum calibration, native particle identity or chiral continuum is inferred.
